brief: brief-js163.md: on processors only the 12-thread node holds the job at 1.2x (1.36 to 1.38x in a quiet pod, all threads allowed, about 7 used); the 6-processor node reaches 1.06 to 1.10x with the whole node and has 94% of its CPU and 98% of its memory reserved; at 4 cores every node is at 0.83 to 0.93x. Both UHD 630s run the job at 4 to 5 times real time. The dogfood's transcode store is a ReadWriteOnce local volume on the 4-core node; docs/transcoding.md asks for a shared volume or S3.
tradeoff: Which nodes carry the dogfood's workers and on what, and which shared store the owner's homelab takes on; each is the owner's change to approve.
entry: JS-166 runs a processor worker on the 12-thread node beside the 4-core node's worker, which stays as helper and failover; no worker goes on the 6-processor node until it can use its GPU. The GPUs of both UHD 630 nodes are used when JS-170 lands and not before: nothing is deployed for hardware jellyscale cannot yet use. JS-166 gains: segment latency between nodes on the chosen store measured first, the freeze bound of JS-168 over three plays, a play beside a subtitle extraction, and each job's speed against its worker's measured capacity. The store goes to the owner as three priced options: an S3 bucket (a service to run or reuse, every segment over the network, workers free of any volume, the object-storage path dogfooded); a ReadWriteMany volume (nothing new if the NAS exports one, NFS behaviour between nodes unverified); or no shared store with the whole pod moved to the 12-thread node (ends the stall soonest, but a bigger machine and not more machines: no helper, no failover, nothing of JS-166 or JS-057 shown). The product is neutral between the first two; the third alone does not show the product. Unverified when decided: whether a worker of about 8 CPUs schedules on the 12-thread node (its reserved requests were not read); a real worker's speed on the 12-thread node (pods ran faster than the dogfood's own jobs by about 0.7 beside an extraction); either store between machines; what S3 or RWX the homelab already has. Data that reopens it: JS-166 measuring the 12-thread worker under 1.0x with the 4-core helper, which returns the task to the product owner and moves JS-170 up. Owner's answer (2026-11-21): the owner left the store choice to the lead and will set up an S3 service in the homelab; the lead chose an S3 bucket (option 1), because workers can then run on any node, which JS-057 and the GPU workers after JS-170 need, while the ReadWriteMany option's behaviour between machines is unverified and ties the transcodes to the NAS. JS-166 uses an S3 bucket and measures segment latency between nodes on it first.
serves: PRODUCT.md: 'Growing is adding machines ... more viewers or heavier films are met by more machines rather than a bigger one.' 'Storage is a per-library choice between POSIX and S3-compatible object storage, with neither a second-class citizen.' 'Failures are invisible.' D-038: the 4K HDR stall is a gap to close, not to accept.
